title: Reef fish bag and vessel limits; Atlantic and Keys gag and black grouper: 1 per person and 2 per vessel combined from 28 Oct 2026
effect: Snapper aggregate 10 per person. Grouper aggregate 4 per person in the Gulf outside Monroe County, 3 in the Atlantic and all Monroe County waters. From 28 Oct 2026, in Atlantic and all Monroe County state waters, 1 gag or black grouper per person per day and no more than 2 gag or black grouper in any combination aboard any vessel at any time. Gulf state waters outside Monroe: no more than 2 gag per person within the aggregate.
excerpt: (1)(a) ... no recreational harvester shall harvest within or without Florida waters, nor possess within or without Florida waters, more than a total of 10 snapper per day, in any combination of species. ... (2)(b)1. No recreational harvester shall harvest in or from all Florida waters of the Atlantic Ocean and all Florida waters of Monroe County, nor possess while in or on Florida waters of the Atlantic Ocean and all Florida waters of Monroe County, more than 1 gag or black grouper per day and no more than 2 gag or black grouper in any combination shall be possessed aboard any vessel in or on Florida waters of the Atlantic Ocean and all Florida waters of Monroe County at any time (consistent with Federal Standard established in 50 C.F.R §622.187 as of October 28, 2026).
note: UPDATED 11 Nov 2026. FLRules shows a new final adopted version, rule file date 26 Oct 2026, effective 28 Oct 2026 (notice 31547424, adopting the 5 Oct 2026 proposal, notice 31448290). The adopted .doc (tid 31547424) was fetched in the author's Chrome from flrules.org and its text extracted in the page; (1)(a) and (2)(b)1. are quoted from that text, whitespace collapsed. The page title reads 'Recreational Bag and Vessel Limits'; the first line of the .doc reads 'Recreational Bag Limits'. The state vessel limit has no charter exception: 2 gag or black grouper combined aboard any vessel at any time, which is stricter than the federal for-hire limit of 2 per trip. Earlier notes said the text in force since 1 Apr 2026 had not been read; that version is superseded.

cite: Fla. Admin. Code ch. 68B-3 (rules 68B-3.001 to 68B-3.050), checked for Laws of Fla. ch. 8636 (1921)
title: FWC has not repealed Broward's 1921 inside-waters gear act (confirmed negative)
effect: No rule in ch. 68B-3 repeals Laws of Fla. ch. 8636 (1921), printed as Broward County Code § 13-5. The only Broward repeal, r. 68B-3.045, removes section 2 of ch. 25714 (1949). Broward § 13-5 is therefore still printed and unrepealed by FWC; whether it reaches salt water is the open question (open question 27).
excerpt: The Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission has determined that the repeal of a portion of Broward County Special Act of Local Application, chapter 25714, Laws of Florida (1949), will not adversely affect the marine resources of Broward County or of the State of Florida, therefore Section 2 of Broward County Special Act of Local Application, chapter 25714, Laws of Florida (1949), is hereby repealed.

cite: Fla. Admin. Register notice 31403864 (23 Sep 2026, Vol. 52/185), notice of rule development, rr. 68B-35.001 to 68B-35.004
title: FWC is developing new African pompano rules, including gear, to move into a new chapter 68B-66 (not in force)
effect: Development only. FWC may change definitions, size and bag limits and gear rules for African pompano in state and adjacent federal waters, moving them to a new ch. 68B-66. Bears on open question 29 (whether spearing African pompano is allowed in federal waters). Nothing changes until a rule is adopted.
excerpt: The purpose of this rule development notice is to address potential rule amendments for African pompano in Florida state waters and adjacent federal waters to ensure the continuing health and abundance of the species. The effect of these rule changes would be to modify management measures for African pompano in Florida state and federal waters, as well as to move rules regarding African pompano from Chapter 68B-35, F.A.C., to a new rule chapter, Chapter 68B-66, F.A.C.

cite: Fla. Admin. Code r. 40D-9.230 (Southwest Florida Water Management District)
title: Water management district lands: no spear guns, and no scuba without a special use authorization
effect: On Southwest Florida Water Management District lands, possessing or using a spear gun is prohibited except during authorized hunts, district land work or under a special use authorization (r. 40D-9.230), and scuba is prohibited without a special use authorization (r. 40D-9.181). The Suwannee River and St. Johns River districts bar scuba on their lands the same way (rr. 40B-9.1381(8), 40C-9.190), and Suwannee River counts spear guns among 'firearms and similar devices' (r. 40B-9.021(14)). South Florida's public use rules close swimming, snorkeling and scuba in its impoundment areas (r. 40E-7.5384). District lands are mostly inland, where a speargun may not be carried on fresh water anyway; the rule matters on coastal district preserves. District land boundaries are not drawn.
excerpt: The possession or use of potentially dangerous equipment on District Lands, as set forth below, is prohibited except: (1) For hunting purposes during specifically authorized hunts; (2) For District initiated land management activities; (3) As authorized by a Special Use Authorization. Potentially dangerous equipment includes blow guns, crossbows, spear guns, or other devices capable of mechanically propelling an arrow, spear, or similar projectile.
scope: Lands owned or managed by the five water management districts (Southwest Florida quoted).
note: Read 12 Nov 2026 in the author's Chrome: all 157 rules in FLRules chapters 40A-7, 40A-9, 40B-9, 40C-9, 40D-9 and 40E-7 fetched and their adopted Word files searched for spear, scuba, snorkel, underwater, skin diving and diving; eight rules matched. The excerpt is r. 40D-9.230 as adopted, effective 15 Jul 2012. SWFWMD published proposed amendments to chapter 40D-9 in 2026 (development notice 26 Aug 2026, Vol. 52/166); the redline keeps the spear gun ban and the scuba rule.
